sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h2 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i02, caller. Medium target, Hard welcome (user,
  2026-10-10: no Easy slot). Edition trap in the aq-00964 layout (event only in the later edition, which
  prints its own newer deadline; the deadline then running sits in the previous edition), with a second,
  independent lure: the later edition describes the earlier order by a label ("15-day comment period") that
  does not give its printed deadline. Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 7 L125 dates Uganda's declaration July 28, 2026. Doc 7 L27 puts its own order in
  effect August 12, 2026; L41 names the order before it (continued July 13, 2026, for 30 days). Doc 6
  L25-27 is that order (in effect July 13 to August 12) and prints its comment deadline, July 31, 2026.
  July 31 - July 28 = 3 days.
- Universe: not applicable (single value).
- Necessity: Doc 7 is the only document that reports the declaration ("declared the outbreak over": Doc 7
  only; the other "July 28" hits are the 1951 Refugee Convention date in Doc 1-3). Without it there is no
  date to count from. Doc 6 is the only document that prints July 31 ("July 31": Doc 6 only, one hit).
  Without it the July order's comment period is known only as "a 15-day comment period" (Doc 7 L41), which
  gives July 28 if counted from issuance: 0 days, not 3. The wording gives no date.
- Selected-lever checks (Python, 2026-10-10): right edition, printed deadline: July 31 - July 28 = 3.
  Wrong edition: Doc 7's own deadline, September 1 - July 28 = 35. Label instead of the printed deadline:
  July 13 + 15 days = July 28, 0 days. End of the order instead of its comment period: August 12 - July 28
  = 15. The June order's deadline, July 10, had passed 18 days earlier. Each route has its own value.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong year or edition, uses the wrong period or date) -> 35 days, from
  Doc 7 L28, the deadline printed in the document that reports the event. Considered and not declared: the
  label route (0 days). It is a real lure, but no trap in the form's list is known to fit it ("Document
  convention" has no saved definition; "Superseded date or version" names an old deadline, and this one was
  never the deadline), and an ill-fitting mode blocks Submit. No measured attempts yet; re-declare from
  observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: Python date difference 2026-10-10: date(2026,7,31) - date(2026,7,28) = 3 days.
  Convention: elapsed days from the declaration to the last day comments could be received ("on or before
  July 31, 2026"); the question asks how many days after the declaration the deadline fell.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints the gap. The page overview lists "July 31, 2026" under
  Doc 6's dates and "September 1"-style dates only as Doc 7's; it does not mention the declaration date.
  Shortest route: find the declaration in Doc 7, see that Doc 7's order postdates it, open the July order's
  DATES line, subtract.
- Precision/readings: the "comment deadline" is the printed last day for comments, July 31 (Doc 6 L27). The 15-day label cannot move that: Doc 6 prints both the label (L260, "a simultaneous 15-day comment
  period") and the deadline, and in all three orders the deadline is 15 days after Federal Register
  publication (June 25 -> July 10; July 16 -> July 31; August 17 -> September 1), not after issuance. Only
  one order was in force on July 28: the July 13 order ran to August 12 and the next took effect that day.
  "Declared its Ebola outbreak over" is the Ministry of Health's July 28 declaration; Doc 7 gives no other
  date for it (July 16 is a patient's discharge; June 21 is the last confirmed case). The wording asks for
  a deadline rather than "when the comment period closed", so a reader looks for the printed date.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md coverage lines).
- Style/set review: 22 words, one sentence, one ask. q01 uses a different event (Doc 6's), another document
  pair (Doc 5 and Doc 6) and a percentage; neither question states the other's order or dates. Sketch i03
  (the rate between the July order's two counts) shares this question's event and is held as its
  alternative, not a second question.
- Warnings answered: see the floor run recorded at hand-over.

sections.question: How many days after Uganda declared its Ebola outbreak over was the comment deadline for the CDC entry-suspension order then in force?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 7, factual basis, section III.B): the Republic of Uganda Ministry of Health declared the outbreak over on July 28, 2026.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 7, DATES and SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION): the order printed in Doc 7 took effect on August 12, 2026, after the declaration. The order in force on July 28 was the one continued on July 13, 2026 for 30 days. Doc 7 says only that it had a 15-day comment period and prints no closing date for it.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 6, SUMMARY and DATES): Doc 6 prints that order. It was issued and took effect on July 13, 2026, and written comments on it had to be received on or before July 31, 2026, so July 31 was its comment deadline.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 6 and Doc 7): both dates fall in July, so the days from the declaration to the comment deadline are 31 - 28 = 3.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Wrong year or edition: Doc 7 reports Uganda's July 28 declaration beside its own comment deadline, September 1, 2026, but that order took effect August 12. Using it gives 35 days. The order in force on July 28 is Doc 6's, with comments due July 31, so 3 days.
